topic.title: UPI never felt like it cost anything
topic.claim: We stopped thinking of UPI as money leaving and started treating it as a reflex, and a 0.4% charge is the first time the reflex has a price tag in the room.
topic.behaviour: Scanning a QR for everything, from the big electronics bill to the small one, without ever thinking about who pays for the rail underneath.
topic.mechanism: Zero visible friction makes spending feel weightless. When a merchant has to pay on a ₹2,000-plus payment, the invisible cost can turn into a surcharge or a 'cash de do' at the counter, and we notice only then.
real_details: From 15 October a 0.4% merchant charge applies to person-to-merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000
Railways, telecom, fuel and insurance pay a flat ₹5 instead
Small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month via QR are exempt
The government says consumers pay nothing directly and about 96% of merchant transactions are unaffected
Average daily UPI volume reached 802 million in September, a first
The Supreme Court declined to stay the rule and asked the Centre to justify the ₹2,000 threshold
topic.news_peg: 0.4% UPI merchant charge above ₹2,000 effective 15 October 2026, after UPI's record daily volume in September 2026
topic.why_now: The rule just took effect, and the first surcharge or cash request at a shop is likely to be this month.

score.why: Names the exact UPI merchant fee and turns a daily reflex into a priced moment, same move as the QR-sticker and GST 2.0 takes he kept.
